threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newbies by how they still stand on the left side of the escalators during Tube strikes, while locals just squeeze past.
Last night, the 59 driver ignored a guy in a unicorn onesie singing 'Sweet Caroline' at the top of his lungs. Only in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy fixing his bike on the sidewalk while a group of kids played football just behind him, I knew this was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you stumble upon a spontaneous rooftop concert, complete with a view of the Spree and a mix of locals and visitors alike.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their bus queue patience; only tourists fume over BART delays while sipping fancy coffee.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni waiting at 16th for a whole five minutes while it played a symphony of squeaking brakes and distant sirens. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the cats on Carrer de Verdi are friendly. Most are dodging crowds, looking for a quiet corner. They know where the real peace is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always stop to take photos of the same street art in Gràcia, while the locals just stroll by like it’s part of the scenery.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop instead of diving into that dodgy kebab shop for a pint. Locals know that’s where the real action starts.
Caught a glimpse of a guy on the 59 bus last night, serenading the driver with classic soul tracks. He actually got a few chuckles, but I think the driver was secretly vibing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy selling homemade sausages out of his bike cart at 2 AM, while a group of kids played soccer in the street. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a club that doubles as a swimming pool during the day. The dance floors get steamy, literally!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows the 14-Mission schedule by heart and can spot a tourist fumbling with the Clipper card machines from a mile away.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo get on the 47, looked like he was headed to a wedding. Just sat down, adjusted his bow tie, and checked his watch like it was all normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think they can just stroll into a bar and order a café amb llet. Here, it's mostly called a 'café au lait' — you'll confuse the locals!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their excitement over the weekend mercados, but missing the subtlety of the siesta hours that leave locals unfazed.
